domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
attributes: id: string (UUID, generated by the repository)
employeeId: string (the requester; always the actor on create)
leaveTypeCode: LeaveTypeCode (canonical lowercase enum value; carried verbatim on the cancellation notification)
requestedDays: number (canonical inclusive count, never re-derived)
approverId: string | null (the recorded decision-maker; null while DRAFT/SUBMITTED; the notification recipient for an APPROVED cancellation)
reversesRequestId: string | null (non-null only on a GP-008 reversal row)
domain_entities.purpose: Aggregate root and subject of every cancellation. This feature adds no field and no state; it adds a side effect to two existing transitions (SUBMITTED -> CANCELLED in place, APPROVED -> reversal) and makes approverId load-bearing as the notification recipient for an APPROVED cancellation. approverId is null until a decision is taken, which is why a SUBMITTED cancellation resolves its recipient from the requester's manager instead.

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequestReversal
attributes: id: string (a NEW UUID, distinct from the original's)
leaveTypeCode: LeaveTypeCode (copied verbatim; the leave type the cancellation notification carries)
reversesRequestId: string | null (always the ORIGINAL request id)
domain_entities.purpose: The GP-008 reversal ROLE of LeaveRequest — a row with non-null reversesRequestId, not a separate table or type. Inserted when an APPROVED request is cancelled, because a completed approval is immutable. It is the row the cancel operation RETURNS, while the notification's relatedEntityId and the audit entry's entityId stay keyed to the ORIGINAL request id. Born CANCELLED, terminal and inert: never submitted, approved, rejected, cancelled or reversed again, and reserves no balance.

domain_entities.name: Notification
attributes: id: string (UUID, generated by the repository)
recipientId: string (the approver — the recorded approverId for an APPROVED cancellation, the requester's direct manager for a SUBMITTED one)
type: string (the existing literal 'leave_request'; no new discriminator)
message: string (human-readable; carries the request id and the leave type)
relatedEntityId: string | null (the ORIGINAL request id — never the reversal row's id)
relatedEntityCode: string | null (NEW — the request's leaveTypeCode, so the approver can act without a second lookup)
status: NotificationStatus (defaults to PENDING on create)
domain_entities.purpose: The existing notification entity, reused, with ONE reconciled addition: relatedEntityCode. The domain slice carried the leave type only in free-text message; the data slice added a generic related_entity_code column so the leave type is machine-readable without joining back to leave_requests. The data slice's option is canonical because the requirement is that the approver can act without a second lookup. message still carries both values for humans; relatedEntityCode carries the leave type structurally. The entity gains no new type discriminator and no leave-specific field.

domain_entities.name: Employee
attributes: managerId: string | null (the direct-manager link; the sole source of the SUBMITTED-cancellation recipient and of the manager-scoped queue predicate)
domain_entities.purpose: The approver identity source. managerId resolves the notification recipient for a SUBMITTED cancellation and scopes the pending-decisions queue for a MANAGER; role/id determine whether the cancelling actor is the recorded approver or an ADMIN acting in their place. No field is added; a null managerId is a real domain case, not a data gap.

domain_entities.name: AuditLog
attributes: entityId: string (the ORIGINAL request id, even on the reversal path)
domain_entities.purpose: The immutable record of the cancellation, explicitly UNCHANGED by this feature: exactly one CANCEL entry per cancellation, same action, same entityType, same entityId (the ORIGINAL request id on both paths), same before/after state, written in the same unit of work. The approver notification is an ADDITIONAL side effect and must not be folded into, replace, or duplicate it.

domain_entities.name: PendingDecision
attributes: status: LeaveStatus (always SUBMITTED while the item is in the queue)
domain_entities.purpose: The approver's own view behind GET /leaves/pending-decisions. A projection of LeaveRequest, not a stored entity: no id of its own, no table, no separate lifecycle beyond queue membership. Membership is derived from the request's current status on every read, so the cancellation that removes a request from the queue is the same write that sets status CANCELLED — there is no second source of truth to invalidate.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Migration: notifications.related_entity_code + leave_requests status/approver_id indexes
recommended_phases.rationale: One migration file. Adds the nullable related_entity_code column to notifications (the reconciled home for the leave type, so the approver can act without a second lookup), the standalone leave_requests.status index (the existing index is (employee_id, status), so a status-only predicate cannot use it as a leading column — this feature's queue query is the first status-only access path), and the leave_requests.approver_id index (recipient resolution for a cancelled APPROVED request and the APPROVED-inclusion variant of the queue). Also resolves the documented-vs-built drift: the GP-008 (related_entity_type, related_entity_id) index on notifications is specified in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md but absent from the initial migration. No service, no route, no repository change.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — Repositories: findPendingDecisions + related_entity_code plumbing
recommended_phases.rationale: Two files. (a) leave.repository.ts: add findPendingDecisions(actorId, actorRole, client?) to ILeaveRepository and PgLeaveRequestRepository (declared inline, the leave module's convention), reusing the existing COLUMNS and mapRow. Predicate: status = 'SUBMITTED' (bound from LeaveStatus.SUBMITTED, never a bare string) AND reverses_request_id IS NULL, scoped by role — ADMIN: no further predicate; MANAGER: the requester's employees.manager_id = actorId; EMPLOYEE: no rows. ORDER BY start_date ASC, id ASC. Read-only: no forUpdate, no transaction. (b) notification.repository.ts: extend COLUMNS, NotificationRow, mapRow and the INSERT for related_entity_code. Unit-testable in isolation through the existing dbPool constructor seam.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — LeaveService.cancel: notify the approver inside the existing unit of work
recommended_phases.rationale: One file (leave.service.ts). Adds the private resolveApproverRecipient(request) helper (APPROVED -> request.approverId read from the ORIGINAL row; SUBMITTED -> employeeService.getEmployeeById(request.employeeId).managerId; DRAFT -> null) and one extra notificationService.create call inside each of the two existing withTransaction callbacks, with the same client threaded through. The notification carries the request id and the leave type code in title/message, sets relatedEntityType 'leave_request', relatedEntityId = the ORIGINAL request id, and relatedEntityCode = the leave type code. The existing CANCEL audit entry is left byte-identical; no new audit action, no second entry. A failed notification insert throws inside the callback and rolls back the status change and the balance release.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — LeaveService.listPendingDecisions
recommended_phases.rationale: One file (leave.service.ts). Adds listPendingDecisions(actor) to ILeaveService and LeaveService: assertAuthenticated, then delegate to repository.findPendingDecisions(actor.id, actor.role). Read-only — no uow.withTransaction, no client forwarding, no writes, no audit, no notification. The SUBMITTED-only filter lives in the repository SQL, so a cancelled request (in-place CANCELLED, or a GP-008 reversal row born CANCELLED) can never appear. Depends on Phase 2.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5 — GET /leaves/pending-decisions route
recommended_phases.rationale: One file (leave.routes.ts). Registers GET /leaves/pending-decisions inside the existing leaveRoutes(fastify) function, mirroring the existing GET /leaves handler exactly: resolveActor(request) -> leaveService.listPendingDecisions(actor) -> reply.status(200).send(rows); on throw request.log.error(error) then sendError(reply, error). No controller file, no role guard, no SQL, no business logic. The path is NOT added to PUBLIC_PATHS, so it inherits the existing registerAuth preHandler. Depends on Phase 4.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 6 — Tests: approver notification + pending-decisions read
recommended_phases.rationale: Two test files, no production change. (a) tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts — extend the existing cancel describe blocks: owner cancels SUBMITTED -> exactly one approver notification to the requester's direct manager carrying the request id and leave type; direct manager / ADMIN cancels APPROVED -> exactly one notification to the ORIGINAL row's approverId; owner cancels DRAFT -> zero approver notifications; the notification create receives the same stub PoolClient as the status change and the CANCEL audit entry, inside the single withTransaction callback; the CANCEL audit entry is unchanged; a throwing notification insert rolls the cancellation back. Plus listPendingDecisions cases (delegation, actor id and role forwarded, empty array is a success). (b) tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.routes.test.ts — a GET /leaves/pending-decisions block over the existing leaveService seam: 200 with rows, 401 UNAUTHORIZED with no actor, and a cancelled request absent from the response. Depends on Phases 2-5.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 7 (optional) — Web approvals queue consumes GET /leaves/pending-decisions
recommended_phases.rationale: Optional, and only if the approver's queue is to be reachable from the UI. web/src/modules/approvals/approvals.service.ts gains a pending-decisions read (or ApprovalsService.listPending switches to the new endpoint) and web/src/infrastructure/api/api-client.ts gains the corresponding IApiClient method. This is the one place the feature touches the second application root, and it is separable: the backend contract is complete without it. Depends on Phase 5.

architecture_md_update:
## Feature: Notify the approver when a leave request is cancelled

When an employee cancels a leave request that was already SUBMITTED or APPROVED, the manager who would have decided it (or did decide it) is notified, inside the same unit of work as the status change. A DRAFT cancellation notifies no approver, matching the existing rule that a DRAFT cancellation touches no balance. The approver's own view, `GET /leaves/pending-decisions`, stops listing a request once it is cancelled. The existing CANCEL audit entry is unchanged.

### Domain entities

| Entity | Kind | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LeaveRequest` | aggregate root, table `leave_requests` | 15 fields, unchanged shape. `approverId` becomes load-bearing as the APPROVED-cancellation recipient. |
| `LeaveRequestReversal` | domain ROLE of `LeaveRequest` (non-null `reversesRequestId`) — NOT a table or type | Born CANCELLED, terminal and inert; reserves no balance. |
| `Notification` | entity, table `notifications` | Reused; gains `relatedEntityCode` (the leave type) so the approver can act without a second lookup. |
| `Employee` | entity, table `employees` | Unchanged; `managerId` becomes load-bearing on the cancellation and queue paths. |
| `AuditLog` | entity, table `audit_logs` | Unchanged by explicit requirement. |
| `PendingDecision` | read-model projection — no id, no table | Membership is derived from `LeaveRequest.status` on every read. |

### Lifecycle states

- **LeaveRequest**: `DRAFT`, `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED`, `REJECTED`, `CANCELLED`. `APPROVED` is terminal/immutable (GP-008); `DRAFT` and `SUBMITTED` are cancelled in place.
- **LeaveRequestReversal**: `CANCELLED` — single state, born CANCELLED, never transitions.
- **Notification**: `PENDING`, `SENT`, `READ`, `ARCHIVED`. A cancellation notification is created `PENDING` and is NOT advanced by this feature — there is no delivery step; `PENDING` is the honest state for a recorded-but-undelivered notification.
- **AuditLog**: `RECORDED` — terminal, immutable.
- **Employee**: `ACTIVE`, `TERMINATED`, `ON_LEAVE`. A TERMINATED recorded approver is still the notification recipient.
- **PendingDecision**: `AWAITING_DECISION` (status SUBMITTED), `RESOLVED` (left the queue — by decision or by cancellation). `CANCELLED` is never a member state.

Named transitions: `cancelInPlace` (`DRAFT -> CANCELLED`, no balance touch, no approver notification; `SUBMITTED -> CANCELLED`, releases `pendingDays`, emits the approver notification); `reverseApproved` (`APPROVED -> original row byte-identical + new LeaveRequestReversal in CANCELLED`, releases `usedDays`, emits the approver notification keyed to the ORIGINAL id); `PendingDecision` `AWAITING_DECISION -> RESOLVED` on cancellation or on any decision.

### Conceptual tables

- **`notifications`** (EXTENDED) — `id`, `recipient_id`, `type`, `title`, `message`, `related_entity_type`, `related_entity_id`, `related_entity_code` (NEW, nullable), `status`, `created_at`, `read_at`. PK `id`; FK `recipient_id -> employees.id`. Indexes: `id` (PK, findById/updateStatus); `(recipient_id, status)` (inbox read, existing); `(related_entity_type, related_entity_id)` (entity correlation — documented in GP-008 but absent from the initial migration, added here); `related_entity_code` deliberately unindexed. `related_entity_code` is generic (a code for whatever `related_entity_type` names), not leave-specific, so the single notifications table stays one concept.
- **`leave_requests`** (UNCHANGED, referenced by name) — already carries `status`, `approver_id`, `cancelled_by`, `cancelled_at`, `reverses_request_id`. New indexes: standalone `status` (the existing `(employee_id, status)` cannot serve a status-only predicate — this is the first status-only access path in the codebase) and `approver_id` (recipient resolution for a cancelled APPROVED request). The queue query MUST also exclude `reverses_request_id IS NOT NULL`: a cancelled-after-approval request is TWO rows, so without that predicate the reversal row is a spurious second queue entry.
- **`employees`** (UNCHANGED, referenced by name) — `manager_id` resolves the SUBMITTED recipient and scopes the MANAGER queue predicate.
- **`audit_logs`** and **`leave_balances`** are unchanged and participate only in the cancellation unit of work.

### Repository interfaces and concrete implementations

| Interface | Concrete | Backing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ILeaveRepository` | `PgLeaveRequestRepository` | PostgreSQL via the shared pg Pool (`src/shared/db/connection.ts`), constructor-injected `dbPool` |
| `INotificationRepository` | `PgNotificationRepository` | same |
| `IAuditRepository` | `PgAuditLogRepository` | same |
| `IBalanceRepository` | `PgLeaveBalanceRepository` | same |
| `IEmployeeRepository` | `PgEmployeeRepository` | same |

New / changed methods:

- `ILeaveRepository.findPendingDecisions(actorId: string, actorRole: EmployeeRole, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>` — NEW. Returns the requests still awaiting this actor's decision: `status = SUBMITTED` AND `reverses_request_id IS NULL`, scoped by role (ADMIN: all; MANAGER: the requester's `employees.manager_id = actorId`; EMPLOYEE: none). `ORDER BY start_date ASC, id ASC`. Read-only: no `forUpdate`, no transaction, returns an array (possibly empty), never null. `CANCELLED` is excluded by construction, which is what makes a cancelled request stop being listed.
- `INotificationRepository.create(input, client?)` — EXISTING, EXTENDED end-to-end for `related_entity_code` (COLUMNS, `NotificationRow`, `mapRow`, INSERT). The optional `client` is forwarded so the insert joins the caller's transaction — the mechanism by which a failed notification insert rolls back the cancellation.
- `ILeaveRepository.create/findById/findByReversesRequestId/update/findByQuery`, `IAuditRepository.create/findById/findByEntity`, `IBalanceRepository.findByKey/update/findById/create`, `IEmployeeRepository.findById/findByManagerId/create/findByEmployeeNumber/findByEmail` — EXISTING, unchanged.

Every method takes an optional trailing `PoolClient` defaulting to the shared pool; no repository opens `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK`.

### Module boundaries

- **Presentation** — `src/modules/leave/leave.routes.ts`. Adds one handler, `GET /leaves/pending-decisions`, mirroring the existing `GET /leaves` handler exactly: `resolveActor` -> service -> `reply.status(200).send(rows)`, `try/catch -> request.log.error -> sendError`. No controller file, no SQL, no role branch, no business logic.
- **Application** — `LeaveService.cancel` (extended) and `LeaveService.listPendingDecisions` (new), both declared on `ILeaveService` before implementation. `cancel` keeps ownership of the unit of work; the approver notification is one more step inside the two existing `uow.withTransaction` callbacks, with the same `client` threaded through. `listPendingDecisions` is read-only.
- **Domain** — `LeaveRequest`, `Notification`, `LeaveStatus`, `LeaveTypeCode`, `EmployeeRole`, `AuditAction` in `src/shared/types/`. No new type is introduced: the approver notification payload is composed inline in `leave`, exactly as the existing approve/reject/cancel notifications are, and `listPendingDecisions` takes no query DTO.
- **Infrastructure** — `PgLeaveRequestRepository.findPendingDecisions` (the only new SQL), `PgNotificationRepository` (extended for `related_entity_code`), `src/shared/db` pool + `PgUnitOfWork`.

### Dependency map

- leave -> notification, employee, audit, balance, validation, policy, shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db, shared-auth
- notification -> shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db
- employee -> shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db
- audit -> shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db
- balance -> policy, employee, shared-db, shared-types, shared-errors
- validation -> shared-types, shared-errors
- policy -> leave-type, shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db
- leave-type -> shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db
- shared-auth -> shared-types, shared-errors
- app -> leave, shared-auth
- web-leave -> web-infrastructure-api, web-shared-types
- web-approvals -> web-leave, web-employee, web-infrastructure-api, web-shared-types
- web-presentation-pages -> web-approvals, web-leave, web-shared-types, web-presentation-guards

`leave` remains the sole orchestrator and the only module that changes. Every edge this feature uses already exists; no new edge is added and no cycle is introduced. No module depends back on `leave`.

### Cross-cutting contracts

**Auth.** `request.user: { id: string; role: EmployeeRole }` where `EmployeeRole = 'EMPLOYEE' | 'MANAGER' | 'ADMIN'`. Identity and role come from a JWT bearer token verified by the existing `registerAuth` preHandler (`src/shared/auth/index.ts`), which populates `request.user` from `payload.sub` (id) and `payload.role`; only `/auth/login` is in `PUBLIC_PATHS`. `GET /leaves/pending-decisions` is NOT added to `PUBLIC_PATHS`, so it requires a valid token. The route-level `resolveActor` helper (reused unchanged) extracts `request.user` and enforces id presence plus `EmployeeRole` membership at the API boundary, throwing `UnauthorizedError` on a missing/invalid actor. RBAC is enforced in the service, never inline in the route: `listPendingDecisions` calls `assertAuthenticated` and scopes the queue to `actor.id`/`actor.role`; `cancel` keeps its existing `assertCanCancel` (owner for DRAFT/SUBMITTED; direct manager or ADMIN for APPROVED). The approver notification recipient is resolved server-side from the request row and is never taken from the caller.

**Transaction.** Cancelling a SUBMITTED or APPROVED request performs, in ONE unit of work: (a) the status change — an in-place `update` to CANCELLED for SUBMITTED, or the GP-008 insert of a NEW CANCELLED reversal row for APPROVED; (b) the balance release — `pendingDays -= requestedDays` for SUBMITTED, `usedDays -= requestedDays` for APPROVED; (c) the CANCEL audit entry (unchanged in shape); (d) the approver notification insert. Repository and service methods that must join a caller's transaction take an OPTIONAL trailing `client?: PoolClient` defaulting to the shared pool. `LeaveService.cancel` calls `this.uow.withTransaction(async (client) => { ... })`; `PgUnitOfWork` acquires a client, issues BEGIN, runs the callback, COMMITs on resolve / ROLLBACKs on throw, and always releases the client. Inside the callback the SAME `client` is threaded to every participating call. `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` appear ONLY in `PgUnitOfWork`. The approver is resolved before the notification insert and inside the same callback: for an APPROVED request, `request.approverId` read from the ORIGINAL row (the reversal row's `approverId` is null by construction); for a SUBMITTED request, `employeeService.getEmployeeById(request.employeeId).managerId`. A DRAFT cancellation notifies nobody and performs no balance read or write. `GET /leaves/pending-decisions` is read-only: it opens NO transaction and forwards NO client.

**Errors.** Errors return `{ error: string; code: string }` via the existing `sendError` helper (`AppError` -> its `statusCode` + `code`; any other throw -> 500 `{ error: 'Internal Server Error' }`). For `GET /leaves/pending-decisions`: 401 (`UnauthorizedError`, code `UNAUTHORIZED`) for a missing or invalid actor; 200 with an array of `LeaveRequest` rows (possibly empty) on success — an empty queue is a valid 200 with `[]`, not a 404. For `POST /leaves/:id/cancel` the existing contract is unchanged: 400 validation, 401 missing/invalid actor, 403 `ForbiddenError` from `assertCanCancel`, 404 `NotFoundError` for an unknown id, 409 `ConflictError` for an already-begun leave or an already-reversed APPROVED request, 200 with the cancelled (or reversal) row on success. A failure to insert the approver notification is not mapped to a new status: it throws inside the unit of work, the transaction rolls back, and the caller receives the underlying error (500) — the cancelled request is never left committed without its notification record.

### Business rules (reconciled)

1. The approver recipient is resolved from the request's status and nothing else: APPROVED -> the request's recorded `approverId`; SUBMITTED -> the requester's direct manager (`employee.managerId` at the moment of cancellation); DRAFT -> none. The current manager is never substituted for a recorded `approverId`, and `approverId` is never used for a SUBMITTED request (it is null there by construction).
2. Exactly one approver notification per cancellation, and only for a request cancelled from SUBMITTED or APPROVED. DRAFT notifies no approver. The notification is not duplicated per approver candidate, not sent to both the recorded approver and the current manager, and not re-sent on a retry (a repeat cancel fails its state guard and emits nothing).
3. The notification carries the request id and the leave type: the request id in `relatedEntityId` (with `relatedEntityType = 'leave_request'`) and both values in `message`; the leave type additionally in `relatedEntityCode` as the canonical lowercase `leaveTypeCode`. On the APPROVED reversal path the leave type is the reversal row's `leaveTypeCode` (copied verbatim) and the request id is the ORIGINAL request id.
4. The approver notification is written inside the SAME unit of work as the status change. A failure to notify rolls back the cancellation itself. The notification must not be emitted after commit, must not be fire-and-forget, and must not be moved to an out-of-band queue in this feature.
5. A cancellation writes exactly one CANCEL `AuditLog` entry and, for a SUBMITTED or APPROVED cancellation, two `Notification` rows: one to the requester (existing behaviour, unchanged) and one to the approver (new). The approver notification is ADDITIONAL — it does not replace, merge with, or alter the requester notification, and it does not alter the audit entry (same action CANCEL, same entityType `'leave_request'`, same entityId = the ORIGINAL request id, same before/after state).
6. A request is a member of the approver's pending-decisions queue if and only if its status is SUBMITTED. CANCELLED is never a member state, so a request leaves the queue the instant it is cancelled. Membership is derived from the request's current status on every read; there is no separate queue record, tombstone, or cached membership.
7. Queue visibility reuses the module's existing role-scoped rule: an ADMIN sees every SUBMITTED request; a MANAGER sees the SUBMITTED requests of their own direct reports (one level, not transitive) and not their own; an EMPLOYEE sees none. Queue membership and decide authority are separate concerns — the existing decide guards remain the sole authority on whether a decision may be taken.
8. When a SUBMITTED request is cancelled and the requester's `managerId` is null, the cancellation still succeeds and the requester notification is still written; only the approver notification is skipped. The notification is never addressed to the requester, the cancelling actor, or an arbitrary ADMIN as a fallback.
9. Self-notification is not suppressed: when the cancelling actor is the resolved recipient, the notification is still written. The exactly-one rule holds regardless of actor identity.
10. An ADMIN may cancel an APPROVED request for anyone; the recipient is still the request's recorded `approverId`, not the ADMIN.
11. For a SUBMITTED cancellation the recipient is the requester's manager AS OF the cancellation, resolved live from `employee.managerId` inside the unit of work. No historical manager snapshot is stored or consulted.
12. For an APPROVED cancellation the recipient is the recorded `approverId` even if that employee has since been TERMINATED or is ON_LEAVE.
13. Self-approval is forbidden by the existing decide guards, so the requester and the approver are always distinct people and no call site needs to de-duplicate recipients.
14. The SUBMITTED recipient is the requester's `managerId` regardless of that employee's `role`. No role check is applied when resolving the recipient.
15. A cancellation notification is created `PENDING` and is never advanced to `SENT` by the cancellation operation. There is no delivery step in this feature; the notification's existence inside the committed unit of work IS the record of the notification attempt. Advancing `PENDING -> SENT` is a separate, out-of-band concern owned by the notification module.
16. The approver notification reuses the existing `type` literal `'leave_request'` and introduces no new type value, enum member, or discriminator. It is distinguished by recipient and message text.
17. This feature changes no authorization and no timing rule. Who may cancel is unchanged: the owner may cancel their own DRAFT or SUBMITTED request; only the requester's direct manager or an ADMIN may cancel an APPROVED request; cancellation is blocked once `startDate <= today` (UTC day comparison) with `ConflictError`. A rejected cancellation emits no notification of any kind.

### Recommended phases

1. Migration: `notifications.related_entity_code` + `leave_requests` status/approver_id indexes (1 file).
2. Repositories: `findPendingDecisions` + `related_entity_code` plumbing (2 files).
3. `LeaveService.cancel`: notify the approver inside the existing unit of work (1 file).
4. `LeaveService.listPendingDecisions` (1 file).
5. `GET /leaves/pending-decisions` route (1 file).
6. Tests: approver notification + pending-decisions read (2 files).
7. (optional) Web approvals queue consumes the new endpoint (2 files).

### Open questions

See the reconciled `openQuestions` list: null `managerId` on a SUBMITTED cancellation; null `approverId` on a legacy APPROVED row; whether the approver notification accompanies or replaces the existing requester notification; confirmation of the `related_entity_code` schema decision; queue membership (SUBMITTED-only vs SUBMITTED+APPROVED); ADMIN queue scope; self-notification suppression; the reversal path's notification keying; and the documented-vs-built `(related_entity_type, related_entity_id)` index drift.

### Stack compliance

TypeScript on Node 20, npm, Jest, Fastify, React (Vite SPA), PostgreSQL, modular monolith. All three specialist slices comply: Fastify routes and preHandlers, `pg` Pool with a `PoolClient`-threaded unit of work, Jest unit tests over the existing `dbPool`/service seams, and a React SPA consumer in the optional Phase 7. No non-stack framework appears in any slice.

business_rules:
Consolidated decision, all eight. The through-line: a missing recipient never fails a cancellation, and the notification set depends on the STATE CHANGE, not on who performed it.

1. SUBMITTED cancelled with no direct manager (managerId null): notify nobody and record only the audit entry — the cancellation SUCCEEDS (200). No transitive escalation, no ADMIN broadcast, no ConflictError. A cancellation is the requester withdrawing their own request; refusing it because the org chart is incomplete punishes the user for data they do not control.

2. APPROVED cancelled with approverId null: skip the approver notification, cancellation succeeds — the same treatment as (1), deliberately. Do NOT backfill in this feature and do NOT assert-and-fail: a legacy row with a null approverId is a known, reachable state, and making it fatal turns old data into an outage. Record the skip in the audit entry's metadata so the gap is visible rather than silent.

3. The approver notification ACCOMPANIES the requester's; it does not replace it. For SUBMITTED and APPROVED cancellations there are exactly TWO notification rows, one per recipient; for DRAFT exactly ONE (requester only), matching the existing rule that a DRAFT cancellation touches no balance. Update the existing 'exactly one notificationService.create call' assertions to 'exactly two, one per recipient' for the SUBMITTED/APPROVED cases and leave the DRAFT assertion at one. Do not add a recipient list to the notifications table.

4. Confirmed: add the nullable related_entity_code column to notifications, as reconciled. Generic, not leave-specific; one migration, no new table. Free text is not machine-readable and the leave type is not derivable from the request id without the join the requirement forbids. Carry the leave type code there and the request id in related_entity_id. The message text may also mention the leave type for humans, but the column is the contract.

5. GET /leaves/pending-decisions is SUBMITTED only — it is a queue of requests awaiting a decision, not a decision history. Order by start_date ASC (oldest first, most urgent). Visibility follows the EXISTING role-scoped rule used by list/getById: an ADMIN sees every SUBMITTED request, a MANAGER sees their direct reports'. Status-only; decide-scoping (excluding the caller's own request) is deliberately deferred to a follow-up, so this endpoint does not grow a second copy of the decide rule. approver_id does not need an index for this query.

6. Always notify, even when the cancelling actor IS the resolved recipient. The notification set is a function of the state change, not of actor identity — that keeps 'exactly two for SUBMITTED/APPROVED' unconditional and directly assertable. No self-authored marker in this feature.

7. On the GP-008 reversal path: yes, emit it. Read the recipient from the ORIGINAL row's approverId and key the notification's related_entity_id to the ORIGINAL request id, never the reversal row's id. The reversal row carries a null approverId by construction, so reading it there would silently drop every notification on that path.

8. Add the (related_entity_type, related_entity_id) index in THIS feature's migration, alongside the related_entity_code column — this is the first feature whose entity linkage on notifications is load-bearing, and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md already claims the index exists. Do not audit the whole initial migration here; fix the drift that this feature makes reachable and leave the rest.

Keep the existing cancellation audit entry unchanged in shape, as the scope states. [BINDING RULE — operator decision resolving: When a SUBMITTED request is cancelled and the requester has no direct manager (employees.manager_id is null), who is notified — and does the cancellation still succeed?; An APPROVED request whose approverId is null has no recorded approver to notify. What should the cancellation do?; Does the approver notification accompany or replace the existing requester cancellation notification?; Confirm the reconciled decision to persist the leave type in a new nullable notifications.related_entity_code column, rather than only in the free-text message.; What is the exact membership rule for GET /leaves/pending-decisions — SUBMITTED only, or SUBMITTED plus the APPROVED requests this approver decided?; Does an ADMIN's pending-decisions queue contain every SUBMITTED request, or only their own direct reports'?; Should the approver notification be suppressed when the cancelling actor is the resolved recipient (the recorded approver cancelling their own approval, or a manager cancelling a direct report's SUBMITTED request)?; Should the approver notification be emitted when an APPROVED request is cancelled via the GP-008 reversal path, and keyed to which id?; The notifications table's documented (related_entity_type, related_entity_id) index does not exist in the initial migration — add it now, or treat the documentation as the error?; An APPROVED request whose `approverId` is null has no recorded approver to notify. The architecture records that `approverId` was only populated on approve/reject in a follow-up fix phase, so APPROVED rows written before that fix can legitimately carry a null `approverId`. What should the cancellation do?; The approver notification must "carry the request id and the leave type", but Notification has no structured payload field — only `message` (free text), `title`, `type`, `relatedEntityType` and `relatedEntityId`. Is carrying the leave type inside the human-readable `message` text acceptable, or does the approver view need it machine-readable?; Does GET /leaves/pending-decisions need to exclude requests the caller may not decide (e.g. a MANAGER's own SUBMITTED request, or a SUBMITTED request whose requester is not their direct report), or is it purely a status-filtered list?; Should the approver notification be emitted when an APPROVED request is cancelled via the GP-008 reversal path, given that the reversal row is a NEW row and the original APPROVED row is left byte-identical?; How is the leave type persisted on the approver's cancellation notification, given the notifications table has no column for it?; Does the approver notification replace, or coexist with, the existing requester notification that cancel already sends?; For a SUBMITTED cancellation, what is the approver when the requester has no direct manager (employee.managerId is null)?; For an APPROVED cancellation, what is the approver when request.approverId is null?; Does the approver notification replace or accompany the existing requester cancellation notification?; Where does the leave type code live on the approver notification — a new column, or the message text?; What exactly does GET /leaves/pending-decisions return, and in what order?; apply everywhere these apply, not in one place only]
auth_contract: request.user: { id: string; role: EmployeeRole } where EmployeeRole = 'EMPLOYEE' | 'MANAGER' | 'ADMIN'. Identity and role come from a JWT bearer token verified by the existing registerAuth preHandler (src/shared/auth/index.ts), which populates request.user from payload.sub (id) and payload.role; only /auth/login is in PUBLIC_PATHS. GET /leaves/pending-decisions is NOT added to PUBLIC_PATHS, so it requires a valid token. The route-level resolveActor helper (reused unchanged from leave.routes.ts) extracts request.user and enforces id presence plus EmployeeRole membership at the API boundary, throwing UnauthorizedError on a missing/invalid actor. RBAC is enforced in the service, never inline in the route: LeaveService.listPendingDecisions calls assertAuthenticated and scopes the queue to actor.id and actor.role; LeaveService.cancel keeps its existing assertCanCancel (owner for DRAFT/SUBMITTED; direct manager or ADMIN for APPROVED). No new role, no new claim, no change to the identity shape. The approver notification recipient is resolved server-side from the request row (APPROVED -> request.approverId; SUBMITTED -> the requester's direct manager via employeeService.getEmployeeById) and is never taken from the caller.
transaction_contract: REQUIRED — this feature has multi-step writes that must be atomic. Cancelling a SUBMITTED or APPROVED request performs, in ONE unit of work: (a) the status change — an in-place update to CANCELLED for SUBMITTED, or the GP-008 insert of a NEW CANCELLED reversal row for APPROVED; (b) the balance release — pendingDays -= requestedDays for SUBMITTED, usedDays -= requestedDays for APPROVED; (c) the CANCEL audit entry (unchanged in shape); (d) the approver notification insert. The scope makes (d) explicitly non-optional: it must be sent inside the same unit of work as the status change, so a failed notification insert rolls back the status change and the balance release. PROPAGATION: repository and service methods that must join a caller's transaction take an OPTIONAL trailing client?: PoolClient parameter, defaulting to the shared pool (src/shared/db/connection.ts) when omitted. The calling service owns the unit of work: LeaveService.cancel calls this.uow.withTransaction(async (client) => { ... }). PgUnitOfWork acquires a client from the shared pool, issues BEGIN, runs the callback, COMMITs on resolve / ROLLBACKs on throw, and always releases the client. Inside the callback the SAME client is threaded to every participating call: repository.findByReversesRequestId(originalId, client), repository.update(id, changes, client) or repository.create(reversalInput, client), balanceRepository.findByKey(..., client, true) (row lock) then balanceRepository.update(balanceId, changes, client), auditService.record(entry, client), and notificationService.create(input, client). BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK appear ONLY in PgUnitOfWork — never in a repository or a service. RECIPIENT RESOLUTION INSIDE THE TRANSACTION: the approver is resolved before the notification insert and inside the same callback — for an APPROVED request, request.approverId read from the ORIGINAL row (the reversal row's approverId is null by construction); for a SUBMITTED request, employeeService.getEmployeeById(request.employeeId).managerId. A DRAFT cancellation notifies nobody and performs no balance read or write; it still runs inside the same unit of work for its status change and audit entry. READ PATHS: GET /leaves/pending-decisions is read-only — it opens NO transaction and forwards NO client; findPendingDecisions takes no forUpdate and no client. The existing list/getById/getHistory read paths are unchanged and likewise open no transaction.
error_response_contract: Errors return { error: string; code: string } via the existing sendError helper (AppError -> its statusCode + code; any other throw -> 500 { error: 'Internal Server Error' }). For GET /leaves/pending-decisions: validation failure -> 400 (ValidationError, code VALIDATION) — the endpoint takes no input, so this is not produced; authentication failure -> 401 (UnauthorizedError, code UNAUTHORIZED) for a missing or invalid actor; authorization failure -> 403 (ForbiddenError, code FORBIDDEN) — not produced, the queue is scoped to the caller rather than refused; not found -> 404 (NotFoundError, code NOT_FOUND) — not produced, an empty queue is a valid 200 with []. Success: 200 with an array of LeaveRequest rows (possibly empty). For POST /leaves/:id/cancel the existing contract is unchanged: 400 validation, 401 missing/invalid actor, 403 ForbiddenError from assertCanCancel, 404 NotFoundError for an unknown id, 409 ConflictError for an already-begun leave or an already-reversed APPROVED request, 200 with the cancelled (or reversal) row on success. A failure to insert the approver notification is not mapped to a new status: it throws inside the unit of work, the transaction rolls back, and the caller receives the underlying error (500) — the cancelled request is never left committed without its notification record.
